items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 24 at 4:14PM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 3 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 6 to 9 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...West Carteret and Coastal Onslow Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Wednesday to
4 PM EST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 PM
Wednesday to 7 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The higher of the high tide cycles will be
during the morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to
bring minor moderate impacts on Wednesday. The worst impacts
are currently forecast with the morning high tide cycle on
Thursday.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 24 at 2:06PM EST until November 26 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of eastern North Carolina, including the
following areas, Beaufort, Coastal Onslow, East Carteret, Hatteras
Island, Inland Onslow, Jones, Mainland Dare, Mainland Hyde,
Northern Craven, Northern Outer Banks, Ocracoke Island, Pamlico,
Southern Craven, Tyrrell, Washington and West Carteret.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A coastal storm will combine with anomalously high moisture, weak
instability, and strong lift to produce areas of moderate to
heavy rain across the watch area. Rainfall totals of 3 to 5
inches are forecast, with locally higher amounts possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 24 at 2:02PM EST until November 26 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 25 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph expected.

* WHERE...A portion of eastern North Carolina.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Wednesday to 7 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A coastal storm will produce strong winds
across portions of ENC Wednesday afternoon through early Thursday
morning.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued November 24 at 1:40PM EST until November 26 at 9:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and
seas 9 to 14 ft.

* WHERE...The coastal waters from Cape Hatteras to Surf City.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
